Counterpoint Research earlier published four reports revealing declines in smartphone sales and shipments across India, Latin America, Europe, and China. Below are the contents of each report.

Smartphone market continues to decline, Apple bucks the trend with growth

Although the slowdown in smartphone sales and shipments is not a recent phenomenon, four reports published earlier by Counterpoint Research reveal just how profound the impact of memory shortages and price hikes has been on global demand.

According to a report published yesterday, European smartphone shipments fell 10% year-on-year in the second quarter, hitting a three-year low.

Even in such an environment, Apple's market share rose by nine percentage points to 34%, tying with Samsung. Chinese brands Xiaomi, Oppo, and Honor all saw their market shares decline, at 15%, 4%, and 3% respectively in the second quarter.

As for the Chinese smartphone market, Counterpoint compiled data from the first 30 weeks of 2026, during which the market shrank by 8.6% year-on-year, noting that "the decline returned to double digits after the 618 shopping festival, reflecting seasonal weakness, compounded by ongoing increases in memory costs."

The firm also pointed out that Apple entered a period of "seasonal slowdown" in July, making way for the new iPhone lineup expected to launch next month, with "a considerable portion of demand" already released around the 618 shopping festival.

Another market experiencing sharp sales declines is India. Counterpoint recorded three consecutive weeks of year-on-year declines following the major online sales promotions in July. During weeks 14 to 31, only two weeks saw year-on-year growth, both during major promotional events.

Counterpoint stated that sales fell 14% during weeks 14 to 31, and Apple once again bucked the trend with 15% year-on-year growth, described as "the strongest sales growth of the period," "benefiting from sustained demand for the iPhone 17 series and the ongoing installment offers."

Finally, Counterpoint published a report today on Latin American smartphone shipments in the second quarter of 2026. The report indicated the market fell 10% year-on-year, with Apple and Samsung being the only two major brands to record growth, rising 5% and 6% respectively.
